claims.text: Approximately 80% cold thickness reduction followed by annealing near 750 K for about 10 minutes will produce a dual-phase microstructure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will improve tensile ductility and uniform elongation by at least 50%.
The proposed treatment will increase elongation from approximately 13.5% to approximately 20% or higher.
The treated alloy will retain a yield strength of at least 750 MPa.
The treated alloy will maintain impact-triggered chemical energy release.
HfZrTiTa0.53 typically has an as-cast or homogenized refractory multicomponent-alloy microstructure before treatment.
Varying annealing time and temperature after severe cold deformation can precisely control the proposed dual-phase microstructure.
The treatment will create a bimodal grain-size distribution containing coarse recrystallized grains and finer ultrafine-grained regions.
Coarse recrystallized grains will enhance plasticity.
Ultrafine-grained regions will preserve high strength.
Coarse grains will delay strain localization and enable more homogeneous plastic deformation during tension.
The ultrafine grains will maintain high yield strength.
Excessive grain growth could compromise strength or impact-energy release.
The proposed benefits apply at room temperature under tensile loading at a strain rate near 10^-3 s^-1.
Prior data for HfZrTiTa0.53 report a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
Prior data for HfZrTiTa0.53 report a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
Prior data for HfZrTiTa0.53 report a tensile terminal strain of 13.5%.
Compression testing after treatment will show no significant reduction in strength.
Impact testing after treatment will show no significant reduction in chemical energy release.

contradictions.description: An increase from 13.5% to 20% is about 48.1%, not at least 50%; a 50% increase would require at least 20.25%.
The baseline identifies 13.5% as terminal strain, while the prediction uses 13.5% as the baseline for uniform tensile elongation. Terminal strain and uniform elongation are distinct measurements.
